zupmxode

zupmxode simulates population pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic models, written in rxode2’s model language, with no C compiler: for locked-down and validated machines, where rxode2 and mrgsolve, which need one, cannot run.

  • A model becomes native code in about 10 ms through zumir’s MIR; rxode2 and mrgsolve take one to two seconds. MIR’s interpreter, the fallback, gives the same doubles 1.4 to 1.6 times slower; every R CMD check leg runs both.
  • Doses are NONMEM-style records, read as PREDPP reads them.
  • Closed forms, the matrix exponential, LSODA or Dormand-Prince, with subjects on parallel threads and the same result at any thread count.

Installation

zupmxode is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zupmxode")

Usage

Five subjects of a one-compartment model, each with its own clearance, after 100 mg into the depot at time 0; one row per observation:

library(zupmxode)

m <- pmx_ode_model({
  ka <- exp(tka); cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl); v <- exp(tv)
  cp <- linCmt()
})
ev <- data.frame(TIME = c(0, 1, 4, 12), AMT = c(100, 0, 0, 0), CMT = "depot")

set.seed(1)
sim <- pmx_ode_sim(m, ev, theta = c(tka = 0.5, tcl = 1, tv = 3),
                   omega = c(eta.cl = 0.1), n = 5)
head(sim[c("id", "time", "cp", "eta.cl")], 8)
#>   id time        cp      eta.cl
#> 1  1    1 3.7507426 -0.19810209
#> 2  1    4 3.4167467 -0.19810209
#> 3  1   12 1.4087652 -0.19810209
#> 4  2    1 3.6758616  0.05807312
#> 5  2    4 3.0649859  0.05807312
#> 6  2   12 0.9753628  0.05807312
#> 7  3    1 3.7673999 -0.26424897
#> 8  3    4 3.4992927 -0.26424897

zupmxode also adds residual error, solves without random draws, and lets an estimator evaluate one subject at a time from R or C; Get started shows how.
